reader.decision: Turn on `touch_on_request` in production now. Do not move the touch into `auth-service` for this fix.
reader.decision_reason: The message rules out a time zone bug and traces the stale `last_seen_at` to `edge-proxy` skipping the touch while the flag is false. The flag is a one-line change and the touch code already exists, so it is the smallest fix that addresses the cause.

reconstruction.problem: Active users are logged out after about 30 minutes. `session-gc` runs every 10 minutes and deletes sessions whose `last_seen_at` is older than 30 minutes. `last_seen_at` stays stale because `edge-proxy/session.py:8` skips `auth_client.touch` while `touch_on_request` is false in `config/prod.yaml:1`.
reconstruction.what_breaks: Active users' sessions are deleted mid-work and they land on the login page. My time zone theory was wrong: `cutoff` uses UTC and `last_seen_at` is `timestamptz`, so both sides are timezone-aware.
reconstruction.fix: Set `touch_on_request` to true in `config/prod.yaml`. The alternative is to move the touch into `auth-service`.
reconstruction.cost: Turning on the flag is a one-line config change and the touch code already exists. The message gives no cost for moving the touch into `auth-service`, and no figure for the extra load from touching on every request.

reader.closing_answer: Turn it on in production. Do not move the touch into `auth-service`.
